title: The most visitors with a habitat pledge

blocks.text: A county parks district picks which trail projects to fund this year. Each project brings visitors (people per year) and protects habitat (acres), and each has a cost; the year's budget caps the total cost. The parks board has pledged to protect at least `habitat_floor` acres this year, and within that pledge it wants as many visitors as possible.

Write `most_visitors(trails, budget, habitat_floor)` in `trails.py`. It returns the names of the funded trails as a sorted tuple, or `None` when no affordable choice meets the pledge. Build the model with MathOpt and solve it with HiGHS (the starter has the solve call and the reading of the answer).

Write the formulation first: the set of trails, the parameters with their units, the decision variables with their domains, the objective with its sense, and every constraint with a label. Then code it.
The tests compare your answer with every affordable choice listed by hand, on their own small instances, so any correct formulation passes. About eight lines.

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from ortools.math_opt.python import mathopt


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Trail:
    name: str
    visitors: int     # people per year
    acres: int        # habitat protected
    cost: int         # $k


def most_visitors(trails: list[Trail], budget: int, habitat_floor: int) -> tuple[str, ...] | None:
    """The trails to fund for the most visitors, protecting at least `habitat_floor` acres."""
    model = mathopt.Model(name="trails")
    fund = {t.name: model.add_binary_variable(name=f"fund_{t.name}") for t in trails}
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(t.cost * fund[t.name] for t in trails) <= budget, name="budget")
    model.add_linear_constraint(sum(t.acres * fund[t.name] for t in trails) >= habitat_floor, name="pledge")
    model.maximize(sum(t.visitors * fund[t.name] for t in trails))
    result = mathopt.solve(model, mathopt.SolverType.HIGHS)
    if result.termination.reason != mathopt.TerminationReason.OPTIMAL:
        return None
    values = result.variable_values()
    return tuple(sorted(name for name, var in fund.items() if values[var] > 0.5))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    park = [Trail("Ridge Loop", 900, 10, 40), Trail("Marsh Boardwalk", 400, 60, 35), Trail("Canyon Spur", 700, 25, 30)]
    print(most_visitors(park, 70, 50))

cases.says: a pledge that the busiest affordable choice already meets returns that choice
a pledge the busiest choice misses returns the busiest choice that meets it
a choice whose acres equal the pledge exactly meets it
a pledge no affordable choice can meet returns None, not an empty choice
